clue.text: Each year the French restaurant's food is satisfactory

blocks.note: per annum, Latin for each year, abbreviated
the feminine French word for 'the'
a good table is the food a restaurant serves

explanation.surface: A yearly verdict on a French restaurant: the food passes muster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restaurant's food' looks like the definition, but the answer means acceptable, not edible fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palatable is acceptable or agreeable, a fair synonym for good enough.

clue.text: Argumentative European with a ridiculous claim

indicators.note: a ridiculous version of something is a nonsensical one, so the letters lose their sensible order

blocks.note: a native of Poland
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome European making an absurd assertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing or speech attacks opinions combatively, so it is disputatious by nature.

clue.text: Memorise play — Noel's first

indicators.note: the first of a word is just its opening letter, so only the start of Noel's is kept

blocks.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's play
opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: An actor told to get their lines into their head before a Noël Coward play opens.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel suggests Coward, but only his initial is wanted after Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn lines is to commit them to memory, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: What Chesterton's man was for 24 hours

definitions.text: What Chesterton's man was for 24 hours

blocks.note: surface: a question about the hero of a G K Chesterton novel
setter's reading: the title of the novel names a single day of the week

explanation.walkthrough: G K Chesterton wrote The Man Who Was Thursday (1908), in which anarchist council members are code-named after days of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's title supplies the weekday, and any day of the week lasts twenty-four hours.

clue.text: With horse one is able to arrive at fortification

blocks.note: a Barb is a North African breed of horse
the Roman numeral for one
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A rider on horseback who can reach the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbican in London takes its name from such a defensive outwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbican is an outer defensive tower or gatehouse guarding the entrance to a castle.

clue.text: Oriental celebration no longer showing vitality

blocks.note: E for East, the Orient being the East
a fete is a festive celebration; the word gives only FETE, and the extra F in front has no clue word: the clue as printed is a letter short

explanation.surface: An Eastern festival that has lost its old energy.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, the clue is one letter short: E plus FETE makes EFETE, and nothing gives the second F, so a word such as 'fine' was dropped by the setter or the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete describes something worn out and exhausted, having lost its former strength and vigour.

clue.text: Botanical part — area where the Garden of England is, mate?

blocks.clueFragment: area where the Garden of England is
blocks.note: Kent, nicknamed the Garden of England, lies in the south-east
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friendly gardener's question about which part of the country Kent's orchards lie in.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is the English county called the Garden of England for its orchards and hop gardens; SE is the abbreviation for south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like segments of a flower's calyx, a structure in plant anatomy.

clue.text: One falling short of ideal standard has second shot near the bull

definitions.text: One falling short of ideal standard

blocks.note: the abbreviation for a second
the inner is the target ring just outside the bull, or a hit there

explanation.surface: A marksman whose second shot just misses the bullseye has failed the ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: The shooting picture makes 'falling short' look like a missed target, but the definition is moral.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinner fails to meet a moral or religious ideal, falling short of what is required.

clue.text: Philosopher makes last point with difficulty

indicators.note: something done with difficulty is forced and twisted, so these letters are wrenched out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker struggling to make a final argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A Platonist is a follower of Plato's teaching, which makes such a person a thinker of a particular school.

clue.text: Stop having gained permit first

blocks.note: let means allow, and 'first' places it at the front
to be up is to be ahead, having gained

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt only once a permit has been secured.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or cessation in effort, so it serves as a noun for halt.

clue.text: Member of US group bringing in new age rule (.

indicators.note: a new version is a remade one, so the letters that follow are put together afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An American club member ushering in a new era of regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing in' reads as introducing something; it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a leaguer is a player or team belonging to a sports league, as in major leaguer.

clue.text: Sweet and loving social worker

blocks.note: fond means affectionate
the ant is a social insect and the classic worker

explanation.surface: Praise for a kind and affectionate social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective in the surface, but it is a noun: a kind of confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft creamy sugar paste used as a confection or icing, so it is a type of candy.

clue.text: Dead spirits showing hairy growths

blocks.note: first meaning: in Roman religion, the souls of the departed
second meaning: the long hair on the necks of horses and lions

explanation.surface: Ghosts revealed by their shaggy hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural names the deified souls of ancestors, while the English plural names the long neck hair of horses or lions.

clue.text: Where diner won't want to see fly having trouble

definitions.text: Where diner won't want to see fly

blocks.clueFragment: Where diner won't want to see fly
blocks.note: first meaning: literally, a fly floating in the bowl of broth
second meaning: the idiom for being in difficulties

explanation.surface: The old joke about a customer spotting a fly in their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: It echoes the old gag 'Waiter, there's a fly in my soup!'
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone facing difficulties or a predicament, matching being beset with problems.

clue.text: Actors taking a holiday maybe— — one on a desert island?

blocks.note: the actors in a production are its cast
people on holiday are away

explanation.surface: A theatre company on vacation, pictured on a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert Island Discs, the BBC radio show, calls each guest a castaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is a shipwrecked person stranded somewhere remote, classically alone on an uninhabited island.

clue.text: Shopkeeper given silver coin, something charged for entry

indicators.note: something offered for entry is put inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a stater was an ancient Greek coin, often of silver
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper handed a silver coin as an admission fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged for entry' reads as an entrance fee, but 'charged' is electrical and 'for entry' says where the particle goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer runs a shop selling paper, pens and writing supplies, so is one kind of retailer.

clue.text: Row not favoured after lunch

indicators.note: not says one piece of the wordplay is to be left out of the other rather than added
after places the removed letters at the tail end, so the cut is made from the back of the longer word

blocks.note: tiffin is a light midday meal, a word from British India
in means fashionable, in favour

explanation.surface: A quarrel that broke out after a meal, with someone out of favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, the same sense as a row between friends or partners.

clue.text: Prevent everyone undermining natural resource

indicators.note: in a down entry, to undermine is to sit beneath, so this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: woodland is a natural resource
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A warning that people collectively are eroding woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to stop something happening by acting first, so it means to head off.

clue.text: Panic follows tricky situation in chess

blocks.note: to tail someone is to follow them
a pin is a chess position where a piece cannot move without exposing a more valuable one

explanation.surface: A chess player panicking after a difficult position on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' looks like a link saying one thing comes after another, but it supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin is figuratively a state of chaotic alarm or loss of control, like a plane's uncontrolled spiral.

clue.text: Bread pleasant? Not one tiny portion

indicators.note: not one says that one, as a numeral, is dropped from the word for pleasant

blocks.note: pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread
nice means pleasant
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asking if bread is nice and being told they get only a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small or meagre amount, typically of money, so a meagre share.

clue.text: Ditch in field adjoining road junction

indicators.note: adjoining means lying next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word beloved of setters
a T-junction is named for the letter's shape

explanation.surface: A ditch in a field next to where two roads meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A leat is an open channel carrying water, especially to a mill, so it is a watercourse or trench.

clue.text: Container with wine about to be brought back

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: retsina is a resinated Greek wine
c is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A wine container on its way to being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a round metal box or tin for storing things such as tea, so it is a receptacle.

clue.text: Famine and destruction above and below river

indicators.note: in a down entry, being both above and below something means wrapping round it

blocks.note: death is the end, utter destruction
the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A grim catalogue of hunger and ruin around a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity, and historically meant a scarcity of food, so it is close to starvation.

clue.text: French bitterness over islands to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going to the north means reading upward, the opposite way

blocks.note: gall is bile, so bitterness or resentment
the Channel Islands, abbreviated

explanation.surface: French resentment directed at islands lying northward.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands sit off the French coast, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic refers to Gaul, the ancient name for France, so it describes things typically French.

clue.text: What hell one suffers in Government offices!

indicators.note: something that suffers is knocked about, so these letters are battered into new places
in places the numeral for one within the fodder letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A civil servant's exclamation about the torment of working in government buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall is the London street lined with ministries, and by metonymy names the British civil service and its offices.

clue.text: Plough with wheeled vehicle

blocks.note: first meaning: the star group also called Charles's Wain, wain being an old word for this vehicle
second meaning: a cart for carrying loads

explanation.surface: A farmer's plough hitched to a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plough is the British name for the Big Dipper, also known as Charles's Wain, so not a farm tool here.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation was traditionally pictured as a cart, and a wagon is a four-wheeled cart for goods.

clue.text: Appends charge to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means spoken out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a tax is a charge levied by the state

explanation.surface: Someone adding a fee that must be announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like part of the definition, but it is the word whose sound gives the answer: a tax is a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack something on is to add it at the end, so appends is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Evergreen tree is split

blocks.note: first meaning: the tropical tree whose dried buds are the spice
second meaning: a past tense of cleave

explanation.surface: A report that an evergreen has been cracked in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The clove tree is an evergreen of the myrtle family, and cleave forms its past tense as clove, meaning cut apart.

clue.text: Common taxonomic groups (Latin)

blocks.note: genera is the plural of genus, a rank in biological classification
the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A biologist's note on widespread classification ranks with their Latin names.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'Latin' look like an aside about naming; it supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: General means widespread or prevalent, applying to most people or things, as does common.

clue.text: Criticise female, the one blamed for man's ills

definitions.text: the one blamed for man's ills

blocks.note: to pan is to review harshly
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone attacking a woman who is made the scapegoat for humanity's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she opened the jar that released every evil into the world, so humanity's woes are laid at her door.

clue.text: The PM's bearing

blocks.note: first meaning: Lord ..., Britain's prime minister from 1770 to 1782
second meaning: a compass direction

explanation.surface: A comment on how the Prime Minister carries themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' suggests a leader's deportment; it is a compass point, and the PM is an eighteenth-century one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North led the government during the American War of Independence, and a bearing is a direction such as due north.

clue.text: Leave something on fishing rod for the fish

blocks.note: congé is permission to depart, a word borrowed from French
the reel holds the line on a rod

explanation.surface: An angler leaving tackle on the rod to catch a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a verb telling you to abandon something; it is a noun meaning permission to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger is a large marine eel caught by sea anglers, so it is a species of fish.
